_comment: Manifest of every generated macro of the paper. scripts/gen_numbers.py turns it into numbers.tex (make numbers).
One ENTRY of 'macros' = one LaTeX macro: name, source (tag of 'sources') or file, key (path into the JSON), fmt, kind,
fallback (placeholder while the value is missing: 'todo' = red [TODO: name], 'tbd' = red tbd for table cells), null
(text for a quantity that does not apply). 'families' are templates that expand to one entry per (item, field);
`python3 scripts/gen_numbers.py --list` prints the expanded table, `--check` lists the placeholders still unfilled.
Paths are relative to ROOT = [redacted: local path]. Full description: docstring of gen_numbers.py.
SOURCES
ex     running example of Sec. 2 (Example ex:running). PROPOSED path and keys: the experiment code has to write the
file (it does not exist yet). Expected content: one wrong-answer complaint on a development log with the three
repairs applied to it, and one why-not complaint under the calibrated thresholds:
log, model, T; edit.{question, target}; complaint.{query, pre_answer, deployed_answer, max_coordinate};
rollback.{n_deleted, edits_broken}; compensation.heldout_changed; heldout.n; rescope.own_requests_firing;
whynot.{query, answer, coordinate, threshold}.
setup  scripts/data/setup_facts.json, collected by scripts/collect_setup.py (listed under 'derived') from the stored
files of the testbed (06_testbed_v3/<log>/metrics.json, per_edit_metrics.jsonl, probe_records_v2.jsonl,
complaints_v2.json), from 10_final/cache (cache_table.json, the key-cache index, the hard-negative rows) and
from the frozen protocol 10_final/PROTOCOL.md. Refreshed by `make numbers`; the docstring of collect_setup.py
says what is copied, what is derived and what is checked.
e5lin  experiment E5, linear side (PROTOCOL.md, amendment of 2026-11-11 01:35): a FLAT file whose keys contain dots
(give each key as a one-element list); what each key means: paper_numbers_doc.json next to it; independent
verification: 10_final/e5_linear/verify/verdicts.json. Registered by the final check of 2026-11-11 for the
six placeholders of Sec. 3 (macros th...); NOT yet used in the text (CHECK_LOG.tex, part II, D9 and Q2).
e1 .. e10  the paper_numbers.json of the final experiments (10_final/<directory>/out/; each experiment also writes
results.json and table.txt). Entries marked "key to be confirmed" were registered on 2026-11-11 BEFORE the
experiment had written its file: file and macro are fixed, the key is a descriptive proposal that the results
agent replaces by the name the experiment chose (paper_numbers_doc.json next to each file explains every name).
e10 (public text logs) had written its file: its entries are {file, key, value} records, read as [<name>, value];
[2026-11-11, results of E10 written: the families Text* and Rel* are GONE; see E10 below].
E10 (results written 2026-11-11): the table bodies of E10 are generated by scripts/gen_tab_e10.py (a derived source, run by
`make numbers`) straight from the summary files of the experiment; the TEXT of Sec. 5 uses explicit macros only: where
paper_numbers.json has the number, under the experiment's own name (source e10, key [name, value]); interval ends from
the summary files (sources e10bc, e10bd); maxima, counts and per-draw values from scripts/data/e10_facts.json (source
e10f: every fact carries its source file and rule); the audit's description of the stream around update 173 from the
audit's misc.json (source txmisc). Disputed cells of the verification (verify/verdicts.json) are not registered: the
screening at 2000 requests comes from the VERIFIER's file with ties apart.
NOT RUN (PROTOCOL.md, amendment R19), hence without macros: complaint streams E2 (d)-(g), E4 on the one-hop, BLIP2 and
MMKE-Bench logs, E11, the integer program. The one-hop limitation quotes the audited description of the deployed
one-hop log only (macros oh*). Removed on 2026-11-11: thCond*, thSstar*, thKept* (Prop. prop:cond and Thm.
thm:capacity left the body), the two MMKE-Bench logs. KEPT although unused: the six macros of the running
example of Sec. 2 that describe the edit and a why-not pair (exEdit*, exReph*): experiment E2, part (e), still writes them.
LOGS ('logs'). 'items': the logs USED IN THE PAPER, in the order of Table tab:logs. Source of the list: PROTOCOL.md,
Section 1 (development logs, working points, unseen logs) with the boundary rule of the amendment of 2026-11-10
17:40. role: dev = development log, wp = working point, absent = unseen. Every item gets the macros \lg<tag><field>.
An item with "in_table": false has no row in tab:logs (the two MMKE-Bench stress-test logs of experiment E4 are
introduced with their results, Sec. 5.4: Sec. 5.1 has 0.8 page); deleting the flag adds the row (8 pt per row).
A log that is built later (PROTOCOL.md, amendment of 2026-11-11 00:55: a third backbone or a further benchmark)
is added as an item, with a group; it is an unseen log.
'not_in_paper': built logs that the paper does not use, each with its reason; their stored metrics are collected
as well (setup_facts.json), so moving an entry to 'items' is all it takes to use it. The collector CHECKS the
boundary rule on 'items' and gen_numbers.py stops if it is violated. A log whose stored files are not complete
yet keeps red tbd cells and is filled by the next `make numbers`.
tag: letters only, used in macro names: \lg<tag><field>, e.g. \lgQAcRel. Scheme: backbone (Q, L), family (A =
AlphaEdit-style, W = MEMIT-style, K = MMKE-Bench), number of edits in roman numerals (c, cc, d, m, mm),
Ten / One for the working points with ridge 10 / 1.
names: how a log is called IN THE PAPER (macro \lg<tag>Name): composed from stored fields by the rule given there;
the name of the testbed is \lg<tag>Id. caption, font, group_headings (default false), labels: layout of tab:logs.
TEXT LOGS ('text_logs'): the public ROME logs on GPT-2 XL (experiment E10). They are the last block of Table tab:logs
while their independent audit ('audit') declares every listed log safe (gen_numbers.text_log_rows); cells: family tx.
STATE 2026-11-12 (W3b): the vision-language experiments are written. Their macros are the entries of group vlm
(one per macro that a .tex file uses; list and names: scripts/vlm_macros.py, which rewrites these entries); each reads
either the experiment's own paper_numbers file under the experiment's key (file + one-element key) or a derived
fact of scripts/data/vlm_facts.json (source vlm; scripts/gen_vlm.py gives source and rule of every fact). The families
hOne, mn, sc, rb, vl, lw, rv, cst, ab (placeholders with proposed keys) are GONE; the sources e1 .. e9 with them.
